data.title: Dicot Pharma receives approval to initiate phase 2b study of LIB-01 in the EU
data.description:
Uppsala, Sweden, November 19, 2026. Dicot Pharma AB has received approval to conduct the company’s phase 2b study of the drug candidate LIB-01 in the EU. The study recently began in the US, and today’s announcement follows the company’s plan to also conduct the study in the EU. The countries included in the European clinical trial application are France, the Netherlands and Sweden. Sweden has now become the first EU country to grant approval. The study evaluates the drug candidate LIB-01 as a new treatment for erectile dysfunction at different dose levels following repeated dosing.

The phase 2b study has begun i US with part I, to determine the highest dose to be evaluated in the efficacy portion of the study, part II. With European approval now in place, the company will be ready to begin dosing in the EU for part II once part I has been completed in the US. Part I is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.

“We are proceeding according to plan, and it is very gratifying to have the first approval in EU in place. This means we can continue preparations to start the study in Europe while part I is being completed in the US. This study design is the result of intensive and focused work to advance the development of LIB-01 as efficiently as possible,” says Elin Trampe, CEO of Dicot Pharma.

The phase 2b clinical study aims to evaluate the efficacy of LIB-01 with repeated monthly dosing and to generate data to inform dose selection for phase 3. The study’s primary endpoint is the change from baseline in IIEF-EF score at week 12. Three dose levels of LIB-01 are planned for inclusion in the study: 25 mg, 50 mg and a higher dose to be determined in part I. The study has an adaptive design and will include at least 200 participants, involving patients with all severities of erectile dysfunction.

For further information, please contact:

Elin Trampe, CEO

Phone: +46 72 502 10 10

E-mail: elin.trampe@dicotpharma.com

About Dicot Pharma AB

Dicot Pharma is developing the drug candidate LIB-01, which will be a potency agent to better treat erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation. The ambition is to create a drug with significantly longer effect and far fewer side effects, compared to current available drugs. Today, over 500 million men suffer from these sexual dysfunctions and the market is valued at USD 8 billion. Dicot Pharma’s business model involves evaluating industrial and financial partnerships during clinical development to bring LIB-01 to commercialization on the world market.

Dicot Pharma is listed on Nasdaq First North and has approximately 17,450 shareholders. FNCA Sweden AB is appointed Certified Adviser. For more information, please visit www.dicotpharma.com.

This is a translation from the Swedish original. In case of differences between versions, the Swedish version prevails.

data.title: Paypoint first half dented by lower parcels revenue
data.description:
In the six months to September end, pre-tax profit fell 19.1% from the same period a year earlier to £16.1m, with revenue down 3.1% to £139.6m. Paypoint attributed the revenue decline mainly to lower parcels revenue following the reduction in InPost volumes.

Underlying pre-tax profit was down 13.2% at £22.3m, while underlying earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation fell to £35.4m from £37.3m.

Paypoint declared an interim dividend of 20.2p per share, up 2%, and said it continues to expect a full-year outcome broadly in line with market expectations.

Chief executive Nick Wiles said: "We have continued to face some challenges in our parcels business, with the impact of the significant reduction in volumes from InPost following the commercial reset and major changes at InPost/Yodel not yet being offset by the strong volume ramp up with the Royal Mail and progress in growing our volumes with our other carrier partners.

"The comparison with HY26 is a particularly challenging one and, having now passed this point, we expect Parcels performance in H2 FY27 to exceed H2 FY26. While this business is going through a period of consolidation, we remain confident the Parcels opportunity for our business and retailer partners remains attractive as we focus on growing parcel volumes through our continued partnership with InPost, further scaling Royal Mail, broadening our carrier mix, and executing on new growth opportunities."

At 1143 GMT, the shares were down 13% at 644.50p.

data.title: Indian refiners' October crude processing rises nearly 2% from a month earlier
data.description:
Indian refiners’ crude throughput rose nearly 2% from September to 5.70 million barrels per day (24.11 million metric tons) in October, provisional government data showed on Thursday.

  • Refinery throughput in September was 5.59 million bpd (22.88 million metric tons)

  • Refinery throughput rose nearly 7% from 5.32 million bpd (22.53 million metric tons) in October last year

  • India imported a record 5.58 million barrels per day in October, up 4.7% from the previous month, as most refiners ramped up crude processing to meet rising local fuel demand, data from trade sources show

  • The country's oil imports from Saudi Arabia exceeded those from the United Arab Emirates in October for the first time since the Iran war disrupted regional supplies, trade data showed, as Riyadh offered discounted cargoes to regain market share

  • India's fuel consumption in October rose nearly 10% from the previous month to 20.49 million metric tons, its highest level since March, data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell of the oil ministry showed earlier this month

  • Earlier this week, India raised export levies on diesel and aviation turbine fuel, while keeping the duty on petrol exports unchanged

data.title: Canada's Loblaw Q3 revenue slightly misses expectations on food retail slowdown
data.description:
Overview

  • Canada grocery and drugstore retailer's Q3 revenue grew 3.6%, slightly missing analyst expectations

  • Adjusted EPS for Q3 met analyst expectations

  • Company repurchased 8.3 mln shares for C$524 mln in Q3

Outlook

  • Loblaw expects adjusted net earnings per share growth in the high single-digits for 2026

  • Company plans to invest about C$2.4 bln in gross capital expenditures in 2026

  • Loblaw expects to allocate a significant portion of free cash flow to share repurchases

Result Drivers

  • DRUG RETAIL GROWTH - Drug Retail sales rose 5.7%, led by strong performance in pharmacy and healthcare services, especially specialty and chronic prescriptions

  • FOOD RETAIL SLOWDOWN - Food Retail same-store sales grew 0.6% as traffic declined but basket size increased; sales were supported by new store openings

  • E-COMMERCE AND NETWORK EXPANSION - E-commerce sales increased 16.9% and 18 new stores were opened, including hard discount and drug stores
